01-11.title: Mets sign Sean Manaea
01-11.description: Left-hander Sean Manaea agrees to a two-year deal with the Mets, adding rotation depth ahead of 2024.

01-11.title: Mets trade for Carlos Delgado
01-11.description: The Mets acquire first baseman Carlos Delgado from the Florida Marlins for Mike Jacobs, Yusmeiro Petit, and Grant Psomas.

01-25.title: Mets sign Juan Soto
01-25.description: The Mets land the biggest free agent in baseball history, signing Juan Soto to a record 15-year, $765 million contract.

02-08.title: Mets officially founded
02-08.description: The New York Metropolitan Baseball Club is officially granted a National League franchise, returning NL baseball to New York after the departure of the Giants and Dodgers.

03-26.title: Carson Benge homers in first MLB game
03-26.description: Mets prospect Carson Benge belts a home run in his first career MLB game on Opening Day, announcing his arrival in dramatic fashion.

03-31.title: Jacob deGrom MLB debut
03-31.description: Jacob deGrom makes his major league debut against the Yankees, beginning one of the most dominant pitching careers in Mets history.

03-31.title: Mets open Citi Field
03-31.description: The Mets play their final Opening Day at Shea Stadium before moving to the brand-new Citi Field the following season.

04-01.title: Pete Alonso's first career home run
04-01.description: Rookie first baseman Pete Alonso crushes his first career homer in just his second career game, a preview of his record-setting rookie season.

04-01.title: Paul Wilson MLB debut
04-01.description: The Mets' first overall pick in the 1994 draft, Paul Wilson, makes his long-awaited major league debut.

04-05.title: Francisco Lindor introduced as a Met
04-05.description: Francisco Lindor plays his first regular season game as a Met after being traded from Cleveland during the offseason.

04-08.title: Tom Seaver strikes out 14
04-08.description: Tom Seaver fans 14 batters in a dominant early-season performance, foreshadowing the Miracle Mets' championship run.

04-13.title: First game in Mets history
04-13.description: The New York Mets play their first-ever game, losing 11-4 to the St. Louis Cardinals at Sportsman's Park.

04-15.title: Max Scherzer dominates in Mets debut month
04-15.description: Max Scherzer continues his scorching start as a Met, lowering his ERA to 1.80 through three April starts.

04-17.title: Shea Stadium opens
04-17.description: The Mets play their first game at brand-new Shea Stadium in Flushing, Queens, losing to the Pittsburgh Pirates before a crowd of 50,312.

04-22.title: Tom Seaver strikes out 19
04-22.description: Tom Seaver sets a then-MLB record by striking out 19 San Diego Padres, including the final 10 batters in a row.

05-04.title: Pete Alonso 3-homer game pace
05-04.description: Pete Alonso continues his blistering rookie pace, sitting at 9 home runs through the Mets' first 30 games.

05-04.title: Matt Harvey dominates
05-04.description: Matt Harvey strikes out 12 in 7 scoreless innings during the peak of his 'Dark Knight' season.

05-04.title: Mike Piazza walk-off
05-04.description: Mike Piazza hits a walk-off home run against the Phillies, one of many clutch moments in his Mets career.

05-04.title: Miracle Mets roll on
05-04.description: The 1969 Mets continue their improbable season with a series win, sitting above .500 in early May.

05-11.title: Duke Snider's last home run
05-11.description: Hall of Famer Duke Snider hits his final career home run as a member of the Mets.

06-01.title: Johan Santana's no-hitter
06-01.description: Johan Santana throws the first no-hitter in New York Mets history, blanking the St. Louis Cardinals 8-0 at Citi Field. It took 8,020 games.

06-16.title: Matt Harvey returns from Tommy John
06-16.description: Matt Harvey makes his triumphant return to the mound after Tommy John surgery, helping fuel the Mets' run to the World Series.

07-09.title: Mark Vientos emerges
07-09.description: Mark Vientos begins his breakout stretch, hitting .300 with power over a two-week span that cements his place in the Mets lineup.

07-14.title: Mets trade for Yoenis Cespedes
07-14.description: The Mets acquire Yoenis Cespedes from the Detroit Tigers, immediately transforming their offense for the stretch run to the World Series.

08-01.title: Mets trade for Marcus Stroman
08-01.description: In a surprise move, the Mets trade prospects for Blue Jays starter Marcus Stroman, signaling a push for the postseason.

09-01.title: Mets wild card push begins
09-01.description: The Mets enter September in a tight wild card race, beginning one of the most dramatic late-season pushes in franchise history.

09-22.title: Mets clinch NL East
09-22.description: The Miracle Mets clinch the NL East division title, completing one of the most improbable turnarounds in baseball history.

09-25.title: Grimace Ball energy peaks
09-25.description: The Mets ride the viral 'Grimace Game' momentum from earlier in the season into a September wild card berth, completing the comeback.

10-16.title: Mets win the World Series
10-16.description: The Miracle Mets defeat the heavily favored Baltimore Orioles to win the 1969 World Series, completing one of sports' greatest underdog stories.

10-25.title: Game 6 — the ball goes through Buckner's legs
10-25.description: In one of the most iconic moments in baseball history, Mookie Wilson's ground ball rolls through Bill Buckner's legs, and the Mets win Game 6 of the World Series against the Red Sox.

10-25.title: Mets clinch the pennant
10-25.description: The Mets sweep the Cubs in the NLCS to win the National League pennant and advance to the World Series for the first time since 2000.

10-27.title: Mets win 1986 World Series
10-27.description: The Mets defeat the Boston Red Sox in Game 7 to win their second World Championship, capping one of the most dramatic postseasons ever.

10-27.title: Subway Series Game 5
10-27.description: The Mets fall to the Yankees in Game 5 of the Subway Series, ending their World Series run. Mike Piazza's deep fly to center for the final out remains one of the most heartbreaking moments in Mets history.

11-02.title: World Series Game 5
11-02.description: The Mets' Cinderella season ends as they fall to the Kansas City Royals in Game 5 of the World Series.

12-01.title: Mets sign Jose Reyes to extension talks
12-01.description: The Mets and Jose Reyes engage in contract discussions before he ultimately departs via free agency.

12-09.title: Mets sign Frankie Montas
12-09.description: The Mets add right-hander Frankie Montas to bolster their rotation depth heading into 2025.
